items.title: Every element of a projectively infinite-rank module over a ring with Noetherian radical quotient lies in a finite stably free direct summand
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement places a single element s of a projective module P inside a finite stably free direct summand, under the hypotheses that the quotient of the ring by its Jacobson radical is Noetherian and that the localizations of P at all maximal ideals have infinite rank (statement lines 39107-39114). The proof is a two-stage reduction rather than a formal consequence of the hypotheses: it first uses an auxiliary lifting result to reduce to the case where a finite stably free summand of R direct sum P contains (0, s), and then, inside that case, chooses a complement K' and splits off a free summand from it by a second auxiliary result, so that the kernel of the remaining projection is a direct summand of P containing s whose sum with R is finite free (proof lines 39116-39149). The two steps use the two auxiliary lemmas of the same section, which are carried as navigation stubs; all the bookkeeping with the complements and the final stable freeness argument are inside the counted span.
